title: Fender Splash Shield Removal and Installation
introduction:
The fender splash shield is the liner inside the front wheel opening. Access starts with removing the wheel and tire assembly, followed by the separate groups of liner retainers.

I use the drawings as a fastener map: magenta identifies the attachments, and blue identifies the shield. The liner is a little raincoat for the wheel well; finding its attachments first keeps removal from becoming a tug-of-war with the coat still buttoned. The preparation and wheel-refitting instructions below are part of this job.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail:
Begin on a hard, level surface with the engine stopped, the parking brake fully applied and the wheels chocked. Complete remote-start disabling first, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. If the menu needs ignition ON, keep a valid key inside and release the brake and clutch pedals: from confirmed ignition OFF, press the start button once; if already ON, retain ON.

For an automatic, establish engine-off ignition ON in the same way if needed, then hold the service brake, press the selector button, select Neutral and release the selector button in the ground-level cabin. With the parking brake and chocks maintaining restraint, release the service brake and press the start button once to switch ignition OFF. For a manual, switch ignition OFF if it is ON with the start-request pedals released; if already OFF, leave it OFF. Hold the clutch to select Neutral with the engine OFF, then release it while those restraints remain secure. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before hands-on service. Keep the parking brake applied throughout.

If ignition state or secure restraint cannot be confirmed, keep the service brake held and obtain qualified assistance rather than toggling controls or leaving the vehicle. An unexpected start can cause serious personal injury or death. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Personal protection and materials
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp edges. Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified lubricant or any cleaning material. Failure to observe these precautions can cause serious personal injury. If using solvents, keep them away from ignition sources: they can ignite or explode and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Hoist setup
items.detail: Keep the parking brake applied and restrain every wheel remaining on the ground while positioning for lifting. With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Use the lifting locations in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631), section 100-02. The drawing locates them along the side sills behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels; identify the actual points by the triangles stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or frame. Incorrect support locations can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Incorrect hoist-arm positioning can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death. Keep the engine stopped throughout this task.

items.name: Check lift clearance
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering-linkage components to prevent damage. With a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped; also avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover.

items.name: If a jack is used during positioning
items.detail: Use a jack with adequate capacity for the vehicle, cargo and modifications on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. After jacking, support the vehicle with floor stands; never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, which can lower unexpectedly. Unintended movement can cause serious personal injury or death. The supplied emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire, not this repair. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper, because the bumper covers will be damaged.

items.name: Wheel condition and seized nuts
items.detail: If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; failure to do so can cause serious personal injury. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut, because it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Do not weld or peen a damaged wheel; a wheel requiring those repairs must be replaced, because wheel failure can cause serious personal injury. See [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Brake dust precaution
items.detail: Do not breathe friction dust or blow it from brake components with compressed air. Use approved dust-control techniques and avoid dispersing residue; it can present serious respiratory and other health hazards. Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). Control dust before disturbing dusty components or beginning mounting-face preparation.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage.

items.name: Clean the mating surfaces
items.detail: Apply the dust controls above first; dust removal is separate from mating-face preparation. Before reinstalling the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its mounting surface and from the mating wheel-hub, brake-disc or brake-drum surface. Make sure rotor-to-hub fasteners are secured and do not interfere with those surfaces. Otherwise, the wheel nuts can loosen and the wheel can come off while driving, causing loss of control, serious injury or death. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

items.name: Lubricate only the pilot interface
items.detail: Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft® High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant / XL-2 only where the wheel's central pilot bore meets the hub pilot—the centering interface shown in the linked wheel reference. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc/drum mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces to prevent component damage.

items.name: Install and tighten the wheel
items.detail: Position the wheel on the hub and install the wheel nuts finger tight initially. Clear people and tools from underneath before lowering. Keep the parking brake applied and restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground. With the vehicle resting on its tires, perform final tightening in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads. The linked drawing shows the alternating sequence across the wheel. Failing to use that pattern can cause high brake-disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

items.name: Required follow-up
items.detail: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; failure to retighten can cause serious injury to vehicle occupants.

items.name: Restore the grounded parked state
items.detail: After final tightening, with the vehicle fully grounded, chocked and the parking brake still fully applied, restore its parked gear. For an automatic, enter the ground-level cabin with a valid key. With the engine stopped and pedals released, press the start button once from confirmed ignition OFF for ON; if already ON, retain ON. Hold the service brake, press the selector button, select Park and release the selector button. Confirm Park and the parking brake hold the vehicle before releasing the service brake. With the start-request pedals released, switch ignition OFF if ON; leave already-OFF ignition OFF. For a manual, keep the engine and ignition OFF, hold the clutch down, select first gear and release the clutch after confirming the parking brake and chocks maintain restraint. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before leaving. If the state or restraint is uncertain, keep the service brake held and obtain qualified assistance.

edits.text: NOTE: The illustrations show the LH side. Removal and installation on the RH side are similar.
edits.why: Use the illustrated attachment locations to orient yourself on the opposite side.

edits.text: Remove the wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly from the hub. Refer to: [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) (204-04A Wheels and Tires, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Removing the mounted assembly exposes the liner and its attachments. The linked procedure supplies the hoist preparation and the wheel-mounting precautions summarized above; separating the tire from the wheel is not part of this access operation.

edits.text: Remove the push-pin retainers highlighted in the forward view of the wheel opening, including those along the forward edge, at the top and along the lower edge. Bring each center pin into the raised position shown in the inset, then withdraw the retainer body.
edits.why: The inset distinguishes the center pin from the outer retainer body. I work through the highlighted locations before pulling on the liner, so an attachment does not get mistaken for a stubborn panel.

edits.text: Remove the remaining push-pin retainers highlighted in the rearward view of the wheel opening. Include the upper attachments, the inner lower attachment and the attachments beside and beneath the rocker-panel area. Raise the center pins as shown in the inset, then withdraw the retainer bodies.
edits.why: This view reveals attachments around the back and underside of the liner that are easy to miss from the forward view.

edits.text: With both groups of retainers removed, lower the fender splash shield out of the wheel opening in the direction shown by the arrow.
edits.why: The blue highlighting identifies the complete liner being removed, rather than the surrounding body panels.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: position the fender splash shield in the wheel opening, reinstall the retainers from the rearward view, then those from the forward view, and reinstall the wheel and tire assembly. Seat the retainer bodies and press their center pins back into the installed position.
edits.why: Refitting proceeds from the liner outward to the wheel. Complete the wheel-surface cleaning, pilot lubrication, initial finger tightening, final tightening and subsequent retightening described above and in the linked wheel procedure.
